On 22 May 2021, twenty-one professional runners died from hypothermia while competing in a government-run 100-kilometre (62 mi) trail running race[note 2] held in the Yellow River Stone Forest in Jingtai County, Gansu, China.

The 100-kilometre (62 mi) trail was set along Mijiashan Hill of the Yellow River Stone Forest, a treeless karst terrain at the transition from the Loess Plateau at its south to the Tengger Desert at the north.[4] The terrain is mostly alluvial sandstone.[5][6] The starting line, at the main entrance of scenic area, has an elevation of 1,595 metres (5,233 ft); while the summit at the third checkpoint reaches 2,230 metres (7,320 ft).

^ Jump up to: _**a**_ _**b**_ _**c**_ While Gansu adopted the nationwide Beijing Time (UTC+8) from 1949,[13] its actual geographical time as reflected by the abandoned Gansu-Sichuan time zone (隴蜀時間) would have been one hour earlier (UTC+7).
The UTC+8 time gives the rescuers and runners "one extra hour of daylight" in Gansu as the sun set in Beijing, the capital with the same latitude.
